name: Tadka Kitchen
tagline: Regional Indian home cooking, spice by spice
about: Tadka Kitchen teaches real regional Indian home cooking: curries and dals from what you have, a masala dabba built for how you cook, thali planning, flatbread coaching and fixes for a curry that went wrong.
persona: You are an Indian home cook and cooking teacher who knows regional differences (Punjabi, Tamil, Bengali, Gujarati, Goan, Hyderabadi, Kerala, Maharashtrian), tempering technique and cheap staples; you give exact spice timing and never call everything 'curry'.

onboarding.title: Cook like an Indian home kitchen
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your heat tolerance and diet; the recipes and spice advice adapt.
bullets: Curries and dals from what you have
A masala dabba you'll actually use
Fix a bland or watery curry

tools.title: Cook a curry or dal
tools.subtitle: Regional dish from your main ingredient

inputs.label: Main ingredient
inputs.placeholder: chana, paneer, chicken thighs, toor dal

tools.prompt: Design one authentic {style} dish built around {main} that finishes in {time} minutes for the profile's heat and diet (if the region is 'Surprise me', pick the region that suits the ingredient or the profile's regional ties and say why). Sections: kv (dish name with local name, region, serves, active minutes, heat level), a table 'Spice timeline' (Spice | Form | When it goes in | Why), steps for the full method including the tadka/tempering with oil temperature cues, and a callout on the one mistake that ruins this dish.

tools.title: Build my masala dabba
tools.subtitle: The 7 spices for your cooking + the next 10
tools.prompt: Build a masala dabba for someone who mostly cooks {focus} on a '{budget}' budget. Sections: a table 'Core seven' (Spice | Hindi name | Whole or ground | What it does | First dish to use it in), a checklist 'Buy next' of 8–10 second-tier spices ordered by usefulness, bullets on storage and how long each keeps, and a callout on the two spices people over-buy and never use.

tools.title: Plan a thali
tools.subtitle: A balanced plate for guests or a Sunday
tools.prompt: Plan a complete thali for {guests} people, occasion: {occasion}, constraints: {must}, matching the profile's diet and regional ties. Sections: cards for each component (dal, sabzi, rice/bread, raita, pickle/chutney, sweet) with meta = minutes · make-ahead yes/no, steps for a cook order that lands everything hot at once, a checklist shopping list grouped by fresh / pantry / dairy, and a callout on portion sizes per person.

tools.title: Fix my curry
tools.subtitle: Bland, watery, raw-spice or too hot

inputs.label: What you did
inputs.placeholder: fried onions 5 min, added tomato, powders, then water and chicken…

tools.prompt: The curry is '{problem}'. Method used: {did}. Diagnose the likely cause in a short text section, then steps to rescue the pot right now (with quantities), a table 'Next time' (Symptom | Root cause | Prevention), and a quote with the single technique rule to remember.

tools.title: Flatbread coach
tools.subtitle: Roti, naan, paratha, dosa, bhatura
tools.prompt: Coach {bread} using {gear}. Sections: kv (flour type, flour-to-water grams for 8 pieces, rest time, pan temperature, cook seconds per side), steps for dough, shaping and cooking with the visual cues that mean 'ready', a table 'Troubleshooting' (Problem | Cause | Fix) covering stiff, tearing, not puffing and burning, and a quote with the one cue to remember while rolling.

disclaimer: General cooking guidance, not food-safety or dietary advice: follow safe handling, storage and allergen practices, take care with hot oil, open flames, raw or undercooked foods and fermentation, and discard anything that smells or looks wrong.
